```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  fig.width = 8,
  comment = "#>"
)
hook_output <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
   lines <- options$output.lines
   if (is.null(lines)) {
     return(hook_output(x, options))  # pass to default hook
   }
   x <- unlist(strsplit(x, "\n"))
   more <- "..."
   if (length(lines)==1) {        # first n lines
     if (length(x) > lines) {
       # truncate the output, but add ....
       x <- c(head(x, lines), more)
     }
   } else {
     x <- c(more, x[lines], more)
   }
   # paste these lines together
   x <- paste(c(x, ""), collapse = "\n")
   hook_output(x, options)
 })

```


```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(tmap)
library(tmap.cartogram)
tmap_options(scale = 0.75)
```

## Cartograms

In cartograms, areal regions are distorted such that the obtained area sizes are proportional to a quantitative variable. There are three types: contiguous, non-contiguous and dorling cartogram.

The extension package [**tmap.cartogram**](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap.cartogram/) provides new layer functions for tmap to create various types of cartograms.

It is strongly recommended to use an equal area crs (see [instructions](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap.cartogram/articles/intro#map-projection)).

## Contiguous cartogram

The shapes of the polygons are distorted, where the neighborhood relationships between them are preserved as much as possible.

Labels follow the distorted shapes. With `tm_labels()`, each label is placed at the center of the largest circle that fits inside its polygon, and it is wrapped, rotated, or shrunk if needed (see the article on [label placement](https://r-tmap.github.io/tmap/articles/adv_labels)). The preset `"inside"` keeps the labels inside their polygons. With `col = "auto"`, each label is black or white, depending on the fill color underneath.

```{r, fig.height=6}
Africa = World[World$continent == "Africa", ]

tm_shape(Africa, crs = "+proj=robin") +
  tm_cartogram(
    size = "*pop_est", 
	fill = "life_exp",
	fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "-cols4all.bu_br_div"),
	fill.legend = tm_legend("Age"),
	options = opt_tm_cartogram(itermax = 15)) +
  tm_labels("name", col = "auto", size = 0.6,
    options = opt_tm_labels(placement = "inside")) +
tm_title("Life Expectancy") +
tm_animate_fast(play = "pingpong")
```

## Non-contiguous cartograms

Here, the polygons are only resized while they keep their shape. Most labels do not fit inside the shrunk polygons, but there is plenty of free space around them. Therefore, labels are moved outside, even when many of them do not fit (`move.max = 1`):

```{r, fig.height=6}
tm_shape(Africa, crs = "+proj=robin") +
  tm_cartogram_ncont(
  	size = "pop_est", 
	fill = "inequality",
	fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "cols4all.pu_gn_div", values.range = c(0, 0.5)),
	fill.legend = tm_legend(""),
	options = opt_tm_cartogram_ncont()) +
  tm_labels("name", col = "auto", size = 0.6,
    options = opt_tm_labels(placement = tm_placement(move.max = 1))) +
tm_title("Income inequality (Gini coefficient)")
```

## Dorling cartogram

Polygons are replaced by non-overlapping bubbles. The labels are scaled with the bubbles: with `tm_scale_continuous_area()`, the font size is proportional to the square root of `pop_est`, just like the bubble diameters. Labels that do not fit inside their bubble are shrunk, or dropped.

```{r, fig.height=4}
tm_shape(World, crs = "+proj=robin") +
  tm_cartogram_dorling(
    size = "pop_est", 
	fill = "press",
	fill.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "cols4all.pu_gn_div", midpoint = 50),
	fill.legend = tm_legend("", height = 30)) +
  tm_labels("iso_a3", col = "auto", size = "pop_est",
	size.scale = tm_scale_continuous_area(values.scale = 2),
	size.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
	options = opt_tm_labels(placement = "inside")) +
tm_title("World Press Freedom Index")
```
